3. Defendant Nos. 1-2 jointly and defendant No. 3 separately filed written statements to contest the suit contending that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties. The positive case of defendant Nos. 1-2 is that during RS operation 0.50 acre land of RS Plot No. 1500 and 0.61 acre land of RS Plot No. 1528 was jointly recorded in the name of Abdul Khaleque Jamaddar and others in RS Khatian No. 670 and on an amicable partition Mozaffar Hossain and others got 0.20 acre land of RS Plot No. 1500 and 0.20 acre land of Plot No. 1528 and while they were owning and possessing said 0.40 acre land settled the same to Amena Khatun by registered patta No. 1259 dated 21-2-1947 and handed over possession thereof to her and on the basis of the pattan and her possession total 0.40 acre land was prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun in separate SA Khatian No. 363. Yousuf Ali Jamaddar and others got 0.31 acre land including 0.08 acre land from suit Plot No. 1500 and said 0.31 acre land was recorded in the name of Yousuf Ali Jamaddar and others in separate SA Khatian No. 730. Moreover, while Kazi Sultan Ahmed and others were owning and possessing 0.22 acre land SA Khatian No. 729 was prepared and finally published in their name. While Amena Khatun was owning and possessing 0.40 acre land transferred the same to Abul Fazal Khan @ Ali Miah by registered sale deed No. 3257 dated 4-7-1962 and handed over possession thereof to him who transferred the same to Sheikh Ramjan by registered sale deed No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976 and after mutating his name and paying rents thereof he transferred 0.20 acre land of suit Plot No. 1500 in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by registered sale deed No. 5498 dated 20-10-1986 and handed over possession thereof to them and they have been owning and possessing the same by payment of rent upon separation of the holding by mutation case. Accordingly, the RS recorded tenants lost their title to .20 acre land out of 0.50 acre land. 

 13. I have heard the learned Advocates, perused the judgments of the Courts below, the pleadings of the parties, oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by them and other materials available on record from which it is revealed that the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1-3 are not co-sharers by inheritance in the suit-jote but they are co-sharers by purchase from the recorded tenants and their successors. The plaintiff filed the suit for partition of 0.50 acre land of Plot No. 1500 claiming 0.1250 acre land in her saham. Defendant Nos. 1-2 jointly filed written statement and claimed a joint saham of 0.4525 acre land and defendant No. 3 filed written statement claiming 0.0250 acre land. Both the Courts below allotted 0.0225 acre land in the saham of defendant No. 3 but she did not challenge those judgments of the Courts. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that defendant No. 3 has accepted the saham allotted to her by the Courts below. 

 15. The plaintiff in her plaint as well as deposition of PW 1 stated that Salim Jamaddar was owner of 0.50 acre land and after his death his four sons namely Abdul Khaleque and others got 0.09 acre land each and three daughters namely Badrunnessa and others got 0.0450 acre land each and thereafter, Badrun-nessa and Kamarunnessa transferred their 0.09 acre land in favour of their brother Ismail who settled the same to his four sons Yusuf and others and thereafter, his two sons who were minors died leaving behind their father Ismail and accordingly, Ismail acquired title to 0.17 acre land and on the other hand Abdul Khaleque sold his share to Sultan Kazi and thereafter, he re-purchased said 0.09 acre land. Further case of the plaintiff that the heirs. of Yeasin, Habibur Rahman and Ismail acquired title to 0.50 acre land on amicable partition among the recorded tenants and their co-sharers and thereafter, they 'transferred the same to Sultan, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddin and Aneruddin by registered sale deed dated 9-3-1967 being No. 3250. The plaintiff produced the certified copy of said deed of sale dated 9-3-1967 which was marked as Exhibit No. 4. The plaintiff did not produce any deed of so-called pattan by which Badrunnessa and Kamarunnessa transferred 0.09 acre land in favour of Ismail and any deed of pattan by which Ismail transferred the same to his four sons. Accordingly, title of 0.09 acre land by Ismail from Badrunnessa and Kamarunnessa and by Yusuf and his three brothers from Ismail has not been established. 

 17. While deposing as PW 1 the husband of the plaintiff namely, Muhammad Lalon Fakir stated, "এস, এ ৩৬৩নং খতিয়ানে আমিনা খাতুনের নামে ১৫০০ দাগে ২০ শতাংশ রেকর্ড হয়েছে কি না জানি না।" He further stated in cross-examination "সুলতান মিয়া, আব্দুর রাজ্জাক, এনার উদ্দিন ও আনার উদ্দিন এস, এ রেকর্ডের পরে জমি কিনে। এদের খরিদের আগেই আমিনা খাতুন ২০ শতাংশ কিনে এবং তার নামে এস, এ রেকর্ড হয়।" From the testimony of P.W 1, it is clear that Amena Khatun took settlement of 0.20 acre land and SA khatian was prepared and finally published in her name and thereafter, Sultan, Razzak, Enaruddin and Anaruddin purchased land. Considering above admission of the P.W1 as well as other evidence, the trial Court observed that by registered pattan No. 1259 dated 21-2-1947 [(Pattan Exhibit No. Ka and Index Exhibit No. Ka(1)] some of the RS recorded tenants and their successors transferred 0.20 acre land in favour of Amena Khatun by that pattan she acquired title to 0.20 acre land and SA khatian No. 363 (Exhibit No. Ga=1) was rightly prepared and finally published in her name and she paid rent to the Government [Exhibit (Kha(3)], who transferred the same to Abul Fazal Kha vide registered deed of sale No. 3257 dated 4-7-1962 (Exhibit Ja) who transferred the same to Sheikh Ramzan vide registered deed of sale No. 8289 dated 18-10-1976 (Exhibit Jha) and upon mutating his name he paid rent to the Government [Exhibit Nos. Kha (4) and Kha(5)] and thereafter, he transferred the same to defendant Nos. 1-2 vide registered deed of sale No. 5498 dared 20-10-1986 [Exhibit ja(1)] and upon mutating their names they paid rents to the Government [Exhibit Nos. Kha (6) and Kha(9)]. On relying upon those documentary evidence the trial Court came to the conclusion that after transfer of 0.20 acre land by RS recorded tenants and their successors they had title to remaining 0.30 acre land and accordingly, by sale deed No. 3250 dated 8-3- 1967 (Exhibit No. 4 = Jha(1)] Sultan, Razzak, Enaruddin and Anaruddin acquired title to only 0.30 acre land. 

 23. In the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia 35 DLR (AD) 216 it has been held that rent receipts are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title. Section 110 of the Evidence Act provides a presumption of ownership in favour of person who is in possession of the property and possession follows title. Moreover, as per section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, every entry in a record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. By producing SA Khatian No. 363 (Exhibit-Ga) defendant Nos. 1-2 contended that the SA Khatian was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun on the basis of pattan dated 21-2-1947 (Exhibit-Ka). Though the plaintiff claimed that said deed of pattan was a product of forgery and the SA record was wrongly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun but she could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the SA Khatian by adducing any reliable evidence. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that deed of pattan dated 21-2-1947 has been acted upon and SA Khatian No. 363 was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun. Though the plaintiff claimed that the title deeds by which defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title to the suit land were forged documents but the original sale deeds were produced by the defendants and those were marked as exhibits without any objection from the plaintiff. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that those sale deeds are genuine documents. The defendants by producing oral and documentary evidence have been able to prove that they have been owning and possessing 0.4525 acre land for more than 12 years through their predecessors before filing of the suit and, as such, they have acquired title to and possession of 0.4525 acre land by way of adverse possession.
